title: Orphan/temporal edges: RAG for recall, AGENT judges the DAG edge — never blind-accept top-k
summary: Architectural correction to the semantic note→note wiring. The blind mechanism (autowireNoteProvider: top-5 cosine ≥0.55 → write context edges) is WRONG because it makes the DAG a cached, staler copy of a RAG query — similarity edges are symmetric+cyclic and don't belong in a directed acyclic graph by type. Correct design: RAG (semantic /search over embeddings) is a CANDIDATE GENERATOR (recall); an AGENT logically ADJUDICATES each candidate and decides whether it warrants a DAG edge and of what TYPE (none / context+direction / supersede). Similarity is necessary but NOT sufficient — two notes can be highly similar yet structurally unrelated (no edge). The edge becomes a reasoned assertion RAG cannot reproduce → dissolves the RAG/DAG redundancy. Same pattern for temporal checks: RAG finds the near-duplicate, agent confirms genuine replacement before supersede. Consequences: (1) daemon stays dumb (embeddings/search only, no LLM in request path) → judging is an ASYNC agent/loop step = the self-learn-judge role; (2) retire/demote blind autowireNoteProvider to candidate-suggestion only; the sweep feeds candidates instead of writing edges; (3) the 178 note→note edges created by the blind pass are unjudged and should be re-adjudicated/pruned. Open: re-judge existing edges vs new-only; supersede auto-apply vs propose-and-surface (lean surface, per 'no auto-resolve'); judge folded into the 5-min sweep. Refines [[note about semantic note→note wiring validated]].
